newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds stable after well bid tender.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds stable after well bid tender.

text.p: Australian bonds showed little immediate response to an aggressively bid Treasury bond tender with the market seen staying reasonably cautious ahead of key data both locally and offshore this week, traders said.

"The short stock was taken out by one player and the 2009s went at the mid-point, so it was reasonably aggressive," one trader said. "I suspect not many people expected to get much at the tender, so that's why we haven't seen much reaction."
By 2.20 p.m. (0120 GMT) the December 10-year bond futures contract was trading at 92.660 compared with a pre-tender 92.650 and Monday's pit close of 92.615.
The A$400 million of the relatively new September 2009 bonds fetched a weighted average yield of 7.455 percent and in the middle of a tight one basis point bid range.
The stock was seen quoted at 7.475/7.435 percent when final bids went in at 12.45 a.m. (0145 GMT).
The A$200 million of April 2000 bonds were taken out at 6.690 percent, having been quoted at 6.735/6.695 percent at final bidding time.
The tender was the sixth instalment of the Treasury's T-bond issuance programme for the 1996/97 fiscal year, bringing supply to over A$4.0 billion out of a projected A$6.0 to A$7.0 billion.
The tender result will be seen as positive for the market given the gyrations of the past few days.

However, with the local November labour force report due out on Thursday, and sandwiched between the U.S. PPI on Wednesday and the CPI later on Thursday, the market could contain its enthusiasm for now, traders said.

The market opened firm after further strength in U.S. bonds on Monday, but pre-tender concerns and some retracement of the U.S. advance in Tokyo saw yields above their initial lows. The 10-year bond futures contract is also finding stiff resistance at 92.670, traders added. --Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
